title: Independent live colonoscopy check records histology-confirmed lesions
summary: Clinicians used the pretrained GI Genius detector during 298 colonoscopies in Singapore. Removed polyps included histology-confirmed adenomatous lesions and 14 sessile serrated adenomas. This independent prospective deployment supports real-time clinical feasibility. Its historical comparison used baseline polypectomy rates rather than baseline adenoma detection, so it does not securely establish the claimed detection-rate improvement or reduced cancer incidence.
ai_technology: GI Genius convolutional neural-network computer-aided detection

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Independent clinical team used a pretrained commercial detector prospectively during live procedures, with subsequent histology and independent video review.
evidence.unknown: A randomized same-endpoint improvement estimate, cancer prevention and broader clinical generalization remain unestablished; clinician selection and a short uncontrolled pilot limit interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: The pretrained CNN flags potential lesions in live endoscopy images for clinician assessment and removal, with histology determining lesion type.
